name: PBR photoreal
summary: Materials follow physics: albedo, roughness and metalness answer one light model, so wood, stone and metal look right in any light. Scanned surfaces, global illumination and ray-traced reflections push game worlds close to architectural renders.

philosophy.core_thesis: If every material obeys the same physics of light, the world looks real from any angle and at any hour.
design_principles: Author every material as albedo, roughness, metalness and normal in calibrated ranges.
Use scanned or measured surfaces for stone, wood and fabric.
Light with physical units: a sun in lux, lamps in lumens, a real sky.
Use global illumination so light bounces between surfaces.
Grade the frame with a filmic tone curve, not a heavy colour cast.
Add small imperfections: dust, smudges, uneven wear.
anti_patterns: Albedo values outside the physical range

projection_and_camera.camera: Free camera with physical lens: focal length, aperture and exposure.
projection_and_camera.framing: Cinematic, at eye height; architectural views in photo modes.

geometry.primitive: A dense polygon mesh, or virtualised micro-polygons.
geometry.budget: Millions of triangles in view; 50,000–200,000 for a hero character.
geometry.edge_rule: Smooth, anti-aliased silhouettes with real bevels.

surface.texture_rule: Scanned or procedural PBR sets with micro detail and wear.
surface.material_model: Physically based: metal-roughness or specular-gloss with energy conservation.

palette.strategy: Natural material colours under a neutral or a filmic grade; colour comes from light and material, not from a cast.
palette.colour_depth: HDR, 10 bits for each channel on output

lighting.model: Physically based light with global illumination and ray-traced or screen-space reflections.
lighting.shadows: Soft, area-light shadows with contact hardening.
lighting.atmosphere: Volumetric fog, light shafts, physical sky.
lighting.time_of_day: A full physical day and weather cycle.

world_and_space.interiors: Fully dressed rooms with real furniture, light and wear.
world_and_space.exteriors: Detailed streets and squares, scanned stone and dense vegetation.
world_and_space.threshold: Continuous; doors open into rooms with exposure adaptation.

principles.rule: Layer sky light, sun, practical lamps and bounce light.
Set the camera at 160–170 cm in walk modes.
Build at 1:1 real scale; a door is 2.0–2.1 m high.
Use volumetric fog to separate foreground, middle ground and distance.

interface.placement: Minimal and contextual; fades when not in use.
interface.type_and_icons: Clean sans fonts and thin icons.
interface.diegesis: More in the world: lights, maps and devices.

canonical_works.work: The Last of Us Part II

emotion.target_response: Presence: the viewer forgets the screen and feels in the place.

avoid_when: The brief wants a clear stylised identity.
The budget does not allow scanned materials.

modifiers.how: Keep the layout; paint light into textures and push the shapes.
Add strong depth of field and a high camera, with pixel sprites.

sources.title: Karis, Real Shading in Unreal Engine 4, SIGGRAPH 2013
